## Active

### D-059 — A library exposes its handler bindings under ILib.methods

> _2026-08-20 · core/blong · active_

`ILib.methods?: LibMethods` was added to `core/blong/types.ts`
(`LibMethods = {[m: string]: LibFn | undefined}`), so a `library()` factory returns its object
DIRECTLY and the conventional `methods` member holds the resolved handler bindings, typed through
ILib. Handlers destructure `lib: {methods = {}, ...}` (the default is needed because the member is
optional) and call `methods.<name>?.(...)`. Libraries do NOT re-export config constants — handlers
read `config` directly and the library keeps only the method resolution plus pure helpers;
`blong-login/sessionLib.ts` is the reference implementation with 11 `login.methods.*` bindings.
Trade-off: members other than `methods` are `LibFn` with unknown returns, so a call site needing a
precise type needs a generic (one place: `sha256Hex<string>` in a string comparison). Verified:
core/blong, blong-login, blong-access and blong-gogo lint green; tap access 37/37, party 15/15,
gateway 20/20, kopi 6/6; Playwright 21 passed.

### D-100 — IPlatformApi gained an optional mkdirSync for scaffolders

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong · active_

Scaffolders must create directories, and the alternative was requiring every caller to pre-create
them. It was added as optional so the browser stub stays valid.

### D-267 — A region in meta carries names, not the log position

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong · active_

The log keeps its own RegionMark with an id and pointsBefore, which describe a place in the
execution that minted them: a position is only meaningful inside the process that assigned it, so a
chain that arrived over the wire from another process would bring a number that means nothing
locally. The mark copied onto meta progress entries therefore keeps the three names only
(discriminator, candidates, chosen), and a report identifies a group by the chain of names rather
than by an id. pointsBefore is deliberately not copied either: it counts points still pending for
the next record, while the array counts everything announced, so the two would disagree.

### D-266 — One progress array on the invocation, replaced outright

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong · active_

meta.checkpoints and meta.decisions are gone, replaced by meta.progress, one array holding points
and branches in the order they were announced. Two arrays could not say where a branch sat relative
to the points: a report groups by the region chain each entry names, and the order is what makes the
nesting visible. Each entry is record-shaped (kind point with name, data and timestamp; kind region
with discriminator, candidates, chosen, values) and both shapes name the branches they sat inside.
No alias was left behind, and the transport field was renamed with it: the JSON-RPC response, the
MLE envelope and the receive codec carry progress, so a caller collects what a callee announced
under the name the callee used. The demo scenarios reach the handlers over that wire and assert on
their own meta.progress, which is what exercised the rename; their run does not complete yet (see
the demo friction and todo entries).

### D-280 — Progress reports double their gap, up to five minutes

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong · active_

The progress reporting of a long step now backs off instead of repeating on a fixed cadence: the
first report comes when the step crosses `thresholdMs`, and each later one comes after twice the gap
of the one before it, capped at `MAX_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS` (five minutes). A step that ran an hour
used to print a line every five seconds, which is the excessive logging the reporting exists to
avoid; with defaults it now prints at 1 s, 6 s, 16 s, 36 s, 76 s, 156 s and then every five minutes.

Two things to know before changing the options. `withProgress` is declared in three places — the
implementation in `core/blong-lib/index.ts`, the `withProgress` entry on the lib surface in
`core/blong/types.ts`, and `ILogger.progress` on the same file — so an option added to one is
silently unusable from the other two, which is what happened to `slowMs` until it was noticed while
adding this one: the runtime forwards its options wholesale, so only the types were wrong. And the
cap applies to the gap, not to the count: a step that never finishes keeps reporting, just rarely.

### D-869 — A stream helper a handler needs is published by the shared package, not the runtime

> _2026-11-15 · core/blong · active_

A route that asked for its raw body is handed the request stream and must enforce its own ceiling,
because a route's bodyLimit is checked while a body that is held is parsed and a stream is never
held. The enforcement was limitBytes in the runtime, and the blob realm imported it from there,
which is the one dependency realm code may not have: the deploy tree has no @feasibleone/blong-gogo,
so the migration Job died at module load and took the pods with it (@@F-750). The helper now lives
in core/blong/stream.ts and is published as the @feasibleone/blong/stream subpath, with the runtime
re-exporting it from rawBody.ts so there is still one implementation and the runtime's own test is
unchanged. A new entry point rather than an addition to blob.ts because the browser imports that
module — core/blong-browser reads BLOB_URI_SCHEME and blobUriParse from it — and node:stream has no
meaning in a browser bundle; stream.ts is therefore server-only and absent from the package root for
the same reason. The entry needed the two things this repository has learnt an entry needs: the
exports map, and a line in .npmignore, because that file starts by excluding everything and a
declared entry that is not brought back ships nothing (@@F-746). The publish guard passes over it.

### D-903 — The vocabulary types reach blong through lukaot's declarations, not its sources

> _2026-11-18 · core/blong · active_

The vocabulary types are re-exported from `@feasibleone/lukaot` by `core/blong/types.ts`, as the
plan asked, but the route is not the obvious one: `core/blong` cannot import lukaot's sources at
all. lukaot exports its `.ts` files and imports with `.ts` extensions, which a consumer may only
compile with `allowImportingTsExtensions`, and that flag is legal only beside `noEmit` or
`emitDeclarationOnly` — while `core/blong` emits JavaScript through heft's TypeScript plugin, whose
`default` condition is `./dist/types.js`. Re-exporting from the sources therefore failed with 35
TS5097 errors before a single line of blong was type-checked.

So lukaot gained a declaration build: `tsconfig.build.json` (extends the package's own, emits
declarations only, excludes tests) and the four export entries now carry a `types` condition
pointing at `dist/*.d.ts` while `blong-dev` and `default` keep the sources. A consumer type-checks
the declarations and loads the sources; the package keeps the properties it had — no emitted
JavaScript, sources published, one format — and gains a shape every consumer can read without the
flag.

What this costs is a build-order requirement: `core/lukaot/dist` must exist before anything that
type-checks against it, so `rush build` (which orders by dependency) is the entry point, and a bare
per-package lint on a fresh tree fails until it has run. The alternative — lukaot importing blong's
types and extending them — was rejected: it reverses the dependency the plan pins, and lukaot would
then need blong's declarations to describe its own error.

`ITypedError` also gained the transport fields the framework stamps on a thrown failure (`method`,
`code`, `req`, `res`) in lukaot rather than in the re-export, because a realm that catches one reads
them there; `params` widened from `object` to `unknown` with the shape, which is the change most
likely to surface in a realm that assumed otherwise.

### D-898 — `ITypedError` becomes lukaot's error shape, re-exported by `core/blong`

> _2026-11-18 · core/blong · active_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

The

gateway, the expected-error matcher and every unconverted realm read the type from
`@feasibleone/blong/types`. lukaot defines it (a library usable outside the framework must own its
contract) and `core/blong` re-exports it, so one shape reaches both worlds and no realm changes an
import. `ILog` and `ILogger` keep their declarations so existing imports still compile, but no level
is called anywhere after this plan; deleting them is deferred.

## Superseded

### D-1006 — A perf run reports a distribution and attaches it through five separable pieces

> _2026-11-24 · core/blong · superseded_

`@feasibleone/blong/perf` keeps the measurement and the reporting apart: a sample set, a summary, a
histogram, a text report and an SVG chart, with `perfWrite` putting both files on disk and, when an
Allure results directory exists, under the `uuid-attachment` names that directory reads, referenced
by one result of its own. The split is what makes the next transport's measurement cheap: a test
times what it likes, hands the numbers over, and gets a distribution, a histogram a reader can scan
without the chart, and a picture the report shows. A perf report is written as its own Allure result
rather than an attachment of a step because the framework's result writer owns step results and a
perf run is not one; the tag `perf` is what groups them in the report.

the module moved to @feasibleone/blong-lib/perf so that blong stays the type surface

Superseded by `D-1016`.
